children: Cisco, a networking and security vendor

, outlined plans with Nvidia for faster optical connections in AI data centers; shares traded at $103.885, down approximately 3.15%, around 11:40 a.m. ET Thursday. The pitch is straightforward: move more data through the same equipment footprint while using less energy per bit. For AI operators wrestling with power limits, that could matter as much as adding more chips.

The proposed USFP module targets 400 gigabits per second per lane and capacity of up to 12.8 terabits per second. According to Cisco's announcement, the design promises four times the bandwidth density and approximately 1.3 times the power efficiency of 200-gigabit-per-lane alternatives. TE Connectivity and Amphenol are helping develop the hardware ecosystem. The potential payoff: connect more computing equipment without piling on extra network layers, electricity demand and complexity.

The valuation leaves little room for a slow rollout. The GF Value comparison puts Cisco 37.45% above its $75.58 estimated fair value, suggesting investors already expect substantial growth. An open specification and multiple suppliers could help adoption, but plans still need to become products customers deploy. Watch production availability, customer uptake and revenue conversion. Better specifications strengthen the AI story. Commercial execution determines how much that story is worth.

title: Cisco Stocks Slip 3.15% as New Optics Targets AI Fabrics
